observations.body: The people ask Aaron for gods because Moses delays; gold becomes a calf, Aaron announces a feast, and eating, drinking, offerings, and play follow.
observations.label: The people make a calf while Moses delays

observations.body: Exodus 32:1–6 supplies aftermath evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: The calf, judgment, intercession, threatened absence, and restored presence remain one damaged sequence without being collapsed into an easy resolution.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Exodus 32:1–6 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: The people make a calf while Moses delays belongs to the breach and intercession movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
